caption: What if you could see the present? You can't, and nobody can. Light is the fastest thing there is, yet your phone's light, just 30 cm away, still takes about 1 billionth of a second to reach your eyes. Then your brain needs at least 80 milliseconds to make sense of it, so it quietly guesses where moving things are now. Look up tonight: the Moon you see is about 1.3 seconds old, and sunlight is 8 minutes 20 seconds old (never stare at the Sun!). A signal to Mars takes 3 to 22 minutes, so rovers can't be driven live. Dhruv Tara's light left it roughly 450 years ago, back in the Mughal era (estimates vary). And the Andromeda galaxy, visible from a dark sky, is 2.5 million light years away, so its light is older than our species. Plot twist: stand 1 metre from a mirror and it always shows a you about 7 billionths of a second younger. Which old light will YOU look at tonight? 👇
